title: Joining the musicians' union in 1952
summary: Union officials stopped the music at the Dew Drop and everyone had to join the union in December 1952.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Were you working... These were all union. You were in the union then?

Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. I got caught at... Before we went on the road, it was 1952. A guy named Howard and somebody else, they came in and dude dropped. We were playing there. And the guy said, hey, stop the music. You got a union card? Union card?

You got to be in a union, man. And everybody in there, nobody had... No one had a card. So we all had to go down the next day and go apply for the card. 1952. I'll never forget that. December, 1952. So then we went down and joined the union. That's what happened.

He wasn't going to sign up. The union was just coming into being, it looked like to me. You know, they were just trying to get their feet on the ground. And they decided, hey, let's go to the club owners and let's go get the musicians. And that's how they built up, from what I can see. But now it's almost down to nil, man. It's not too much. Most of the guys on Boydman Street paying for little or nothing, you know. Paying so much a set. And they pass their hat around, you know. But the way we're at, the place where I am, we're on the union. On the union scales.
